A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NiNo research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched across the revised numbering and layout, including Appendices A.1–A.7 in v1 and A.1–A.9 in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization experiments on nine vision and language tasks, component ablations, scaling analyses and neuron-permutation experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds Llama3-style language-model results, learning-rate sensitivity results and an ImageNet experiment.

M1.justification: The graph construction, GNN, prediction loss, layerwise scaling and k-decay remain intact. V3 introduces targeted inference adaptations: ImageNet predictions use a 0.1 multiplier on parameter deltas and sample 5% of graph edges (A.8.2). The Llama experiment uses the previously studied variant without word-position features; Table 7 also documents edge sampling for large-model inference.

E1.justification: V3 adds ImageNet classification with 32×32 images (A.8.2), extending the existing image-classification coverage while retaining FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10/100, LM1B and WikiText103. The new Llama experiments reuse WikiText103 and next-token prediction, so their architectural changes do not independently expand task coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain Adam/AdamW, Linefit, Linefit+, WNN, WNN+, naive-graph NiNo and the evaluated L2O model. L2O/FM16 is a clarified name for the existing pretrained comparator. The new Llama and ImageNet experiments compare against the already used AdamW baseline.

E3.justification: V3 adds substantial evaluation configurations: a roughly 111M-parameter Llama3-style model with its tokenizer, five learning rates, and an 11M-parameter ImageNet ViT trained for 50 epochs with specified preprocessing and optimizer settings (5.2, A.8). The original nine-task targets, evaluation frequencies and training settings remain unchanged; these are additional protocols.

E4.justification: A.8.1 adds a focused sensitivity study testing whether NiNo transfers from the meta-training learning rate of 2e-4 to other learning rates. Figure 10 also extends training-loss distribution plots to vision trajectories. The original component ablations, scaling studies, permutation experiment and PCA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V3 extends explicit dispersion reporting to evaluation perplexities: Table 4 reports three-run means and standard deviations, and A.8.1 describes variability across three runs. The original median-step reporting with ten vision runs and three language runs remains unchanged; no increase in those existing run counts is established.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their results, including NiNo's 48.9% average speedup. New results include Llama perplexity of 22.37 versus AdamW's 24.44 at 14,000 steps, learning-rate-dependent speedups of 14–36%, and ImageNet accuracy of 50.4% versus 49.6%. V3 Table 7 replaces and extends v1 Table 6's cost estimates; identical measurement conditions across versions are not established.

T1.justification: The permutation arguments, mathematical definitions, losses and Linefit derivations are retained. The expanded GNN formulation in the main text restates material already documented in v1 Appendix A.5. No new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, four stated contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: graph-based periodic parameter prediction, improved Transformer symmetry modeling, horizon conditioning and training acceleration up to about 50%. Explicitly naming WNN in the revised abstract clarifies attribution without changing these claims.

C2.justification: V3 explains why shared graph embeddings help compare different architectures and distinguish parameters with similar losses but potentially different downstream behavior (5.3). It also discusses the potentially suboptimal default learning rate, divergence and memory constraints requiring adaptations, and the hardware/software dependence of cost estimates (A.8, Table 7).

D1.justification: A.9 adds pseudocode for checkpoint collection, NiNo training and optimizer-wrapper usage. V3 also specifies PCA fitting procedures, new experiment hyperparameters, A100 hardware and inference sampling details. The code/model access link is retained. The new pseudocode is not fully consistent with the setup: its uniform 10,000-step collection loop differs from the reported approximately 24,000-step LM1B budget.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations supporting Llama3, ImageNet, graph positional encoding, learned-optimizer resource tradeoffs and downstream interpretations, including Dubey, Russakovsky, Dwivedi, Metz and Liu. It clarifies its relationship to WNN and prior neural graphs. Numerous other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract, expands selected GNN and PCA explanations, clarifies baseline terminology, and separates edge/node features into Section 4.2. It adds appendix subsections and updates publication headers, while retaining the overall narrative and most existing prose.

P2.justification: The original PCA display labeled Table 4 becomes annotated Figure 7 and separate Figure 8. V3 redraws diagrams, expands graph examples and loss histograms, adds Llama and learning-rate tables, and substantially restructures the computational-cost table. These changes materially revise the visual presentation beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The learning-rate sweep addresses whether gains depend on the fixed baseline learning rate, while Llama and ImageNet experiments strengthen evidence for transfer beyond v1's evaluated architectures and data. Clearer figures and implementation disclosures improve assessability. The gains are incremental: ImageNet uses adapted inference with limited uncertainty reporting, and the added checkpoint pseudocode contains a budget mismatch with the setup.
